title: Filtering, sorting, paging, grouping
summary: Where, OrderBy and ThenBy, Skip and Take, string matching, and GroupBy with aggregates in SQL.

steps.title: Filtering and sorting
body: `Where` conditions combine with `&&`, `||` and `!`, and many methods translate:
Sort with `OrderBy`, then break ties with `ThenBy`. Calling `OrderBy` twice **replaces** the first sort; it does not add to it.
> **Tip:** `Where` calls can be stacked: `query = query.Where(...)` inside `if`s is how you build a search form with optional filters. Each condition is ANDed in.

steps.title: Paging
body: Show 20 rows at a time with `Skip` and `Take`:
.OrderBy(b => b.Title).ThenBy(b => b.Id)     // a stable, unique order

**Always sort before paging.** Without `ORDER BY`, the database may return rows in any order, so page 2 can repeat a row from page 1 or skip one. And make the order **unique** (end with the key): two books with the same title must not swap places between requests.
Module 7 shows why `OFFSET` gets slow on deep pages and what to do instead.

steps.title: Grouping
body: `GroupBy` followed by a `Select` of aggregates becomes SQL `GROUP BY`:
.Select(g => new { Genre = g.Key, Count = g.Count(), Pages = g.Sum(b => b.Pages) })

Group by a navigation's property (`b.Author.Country`) and EF Core adds the join. What does **not** translate is asking for the grouped rows themselves (`g.ToList()` inside the `Select`): SQL `GROUP BY` returns one row per group, not the members.

steps.title: Search with optional filters
prompt: The tests give you the model from the last lesson:
class Author { int Id; string Name; string Country; List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { int Id; string Title; int Year; int Pages; string Genre; int AuthorId; Author Author; }

The tests fill it with five books: Earthsea (Le Guin, 1968, 183 pages, Fantasy), The Dispossessed (Le Guin, 1974, 387, SciFi), Dune (Herbert, 1965, 412, SciFi), Emma (Austen, 1815, 474, Classic) and Persuasion (Austen, 1817, 249, Classic). Le Guin and Herbert are from the US, Austen from the UK.
Write `List<string> Search(LibraryDb db, string? term, string? genre, int page, int pageSize)`:
- `term` (if not null): the title contains it, ignoring case (compare `ToLower()` of both),
Build the query step by step: start from `db.Books`, add a `Where` for each filter that was given, then sort and page. Everything must run in SQL.
starter: List<string> Search(LibraryDb db, string? term, string? genre, int page, int pageSize)
solution: List<string> Search(LibraryDb db, string? term, string? genre, int page, int pageSize)
if (genre is not null) query = query.Where(b => b.Genre == genre);
template: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
Dojo.Eq("everything, page 1 of 2", new List<string> { "Dune", "Earthsea" }, Search(dojoDb, null, null, 1, 2));
Dojo.Eq("everything, page 3 of 2", new List<string> { "The Dispossessed" }, Search(dojoDb, null, null, 3, 2));
Dojo.Check("pages in SQL", LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("LIMIT") && LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("OFFSET"), LibraryDb.LastSql);
Dojo.Eq("term 'SEA' ignores case", new List<string> { "Earthsea" }, Search(dojoDb, "SEA", null, 1, 10));
Dojo.Eq("genre Classic", new List<string> { "Emma", "Persuasion" }, Search(dojoDb, null, "Classic", 1, 10));
Dojo.Eq("term 'e' and genre SciFi", new List<string> { "Dune", "The Dispossessed" }, Search(dojoDb, "e", "SciFi", 1, 10));
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;

protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=search.db").LogTo((id, level) => id == RelationalEventId.CommandExecuted, e => { Commands++; LastSql = ((CommandExecutedEventData)e).Command.CommandText; });
